images.filename: Footbridge across the lower Afon Cwm Edno - geograph.org.uk - 203085.jpg
images.caption: Footbridge across the lower Afon Cwm Edno. This shaky looking footbridge is actually quite robust!  It is at the end of a disused farm track from Blaenau Dolwyddelan, which does not continue north of the river.  On the 1940s map, there is a small reservoir just west of this place, so the track may have provided access to it.  There is no reservoir there now.  All of this square is rough moorland, wet in places.  The river runs along the southern edge of the square.  The land slopes northward, with Cribau, the SW spur of Moel Siabod (the peak shown in the background) in the NW corner.

images.filename: A Roman Machine Gun Post^ - geograph.org.uk - 218306.jpg
images.caption: A Roman Machine Gun Post? A World War II Home Guard pill box built into the north-eastern rampart of a Roman marching fort. This post guarded against an enemy advance from the east along the Gwryd Pass. A similar pill box is sited at the south-western corner of the fort to provide fire against troops moving up Nant Gwynant. The mountain in the background is Moel Siabod and in the middleground is the s.w. corner of Llyn Lockwood.
images.alt: A Roman Machine Gun Post? A World War II Home Guard pill box built into the north-eastern rampart of a Roman marching fort. images.caption: Creigiau'r Garth. The main feature in this photograph are the heather clad rocky outcrops of volcanic rock, known as Creigiau'r Garth (Garth Rocks), which lie below the yellow coloured grassy upper slope of Moel Siabod. Beyond Llynnau Mymbyr and the A4086 is the boggy Cefn Capel ridge, while the southern Carneddau form a majestic backcloth to the scene

images.caption: Fferm Cwm-Clorad-Isaf Farm. Here the farmhouse of Cwm-Clorad-Isaf (Lower-Cwm-Clorad), situated on a rocky knoll above the flood plain of the Nant-y-Gwyryd and protected  by a coniferous windbreak, is seen from the fescue covered upper slopes of Moel Siabod which provide good summer grazing for sheep.

images.filename: Awyrlun o Gastell y Bere yn Hydref 2024 - Aerial image of Welsh castle Castell y Bere near Tywyn, Gwynedd, Wales 50.png
images.caption:
Castell y Bere, Dyffryn Dysyni, Gwynedd, Wales from the direction of Tywyn.
Castell y Bere is a Welsh castle in south Gwynedd, Wales. It was one of the most important castles of the princes of Gwynedd in the 13th century. It was built by Llywelyn the Great to keep out the invading English. It is believed that the poet Gruffudd ab yr Ynad Goch composed his famous elegy for Prince Llywelyn ap Gruffudd (Llywelyn II) in Castell y Bere in December 1282 or early 1283.
images.alt:
Castell y Bere, Dyffryn Dysyni, Gwynedd, Wales from the direction of Tywyn.
